steps.caption: Net Tools shows the selected adapter, its live address, link speed and DNS
Click a preset to switch. The adapter changes in about a second
Back to automatic addressing (DHCP) with one click, or press 0
Each preset has its own key: press 2 or click to switch to Site A cameras
Save the networks you work on as presets
Give it a name
Enter the IP address
Type the mask as 255.255.255.0 or simply /24
Gateway and DNS are optional, and the subnet is checked as you type
Save, and the new preset is ready on its own tile with its own key
Shortcuts can be reassigned, turned off, or made to work from any app
Close the shortcuts window

chapters.title: DHCP pool for cameras

steps.caption: Open the DHCP pool page
Choose the network to serve. The server address and range fill in for you
Start the pool, plug in the cameras, and watch them get addresses
Pin a camera to its planned address with a reservation
Name it so everyone knows which camera it is
Set the address it should always get
The camera moves to its reserved address at its next renewal
Stop the pool and the adapter goes back to how it was

chapters.subtitle: Hand out addresses when there is no router

chapters.title: Scan and find cameras

steps.caption: Open the Scan page
Use adapter fills in the network you are plugged into
Scan: each device shows its maker, address, response time and open ports
A camera still on its factory address? Reach it adds a matching IP so you can open it

chapters.subtitle: Every device on the network, even on other subnets

chapters.title: Monitor a whole site

steps.caption: Open the Monitor page
Add everything from the scan with one click
Start watching: every device is pinged once a second
If a device stops answering, it turns red and you get an alert straight away
When it comes back, Net Tools tells you how long it was down

chapters.subtitle: Live latency and an alert the moment a device drops

chapters.title: Troubleshooting tools

steps.caption: Open the Tools page
Check which ports a device has open
Open ports are shown by name: web, RTSP video, Hikvision SDK and more
Prove a camera is serving video, without playing it
Net Tools reads the stream details: codec and audio, with camera login if needed
Trace the route to any address, from the adapter you chose
Each hop and its response time appear as they are found
Link health shows traffic, errors and dropped packets on the cable

chapters.subtitle: Ports, video streams, routes, DNS and cable health
